root_cause: Merged PR #4075 changed a canonical Supabase migration. The migration became APPLIED in production, but the post-merge terminalizer read the PR body once before a Terminal-Supabase-Migration-Readback marker existed. It failed with SUPABASE_MIGRATION_PROVIDER_READBACK_MISSING even though the provider later showed the migration as applied. Manual marker writeback plus a failed-job rerun closed the incident, proving the missing piece was evidence orchestration rather than runtime correctness.
prevention: Reuse the existing Supabase production-authority workflow instead of adding another scheduler or runtime.
On protected-main migration changes, query the Supabase Management API migration history with the existing production access token and require exact version plus exact migration name.
Write the canonical Terminal-Supabase-Migration-Readback marker back to the merged PR automatically.
Make the terminalizer wait in a bounded 24x5-second window for the canonical marker so push-side provider attestation and pull-request terminalization can converge without a race.
Keep the terminalizer fail-closed when the exact migration never appears in provider history.
Never treat repository presence, preview success or migration filename alone as production proof.
